note: Des Moines County Conservation park on a Mississippi River backwater lake at the far north end of the county near Oakville, with a boat ramp, dock and fish-cleaning station, a shelter and a playground. Gravel access road. Site 23 sits at the tip of the point on the open lakeshore; 24-26 face the lake across a shore drive. --Claude
summary: Rates ($25 electric / $10 primitive), 46 sites, FCFS self-register, 14-day max, water/dump/outhouses confirmed on the county page. Lakefront kept on site 23; 24-26 and 27 are view only. Pin is on the campground.
flags: WATERFRONT (lakefront kept, on one site): the backwater lake east of the campground is about 300 m across and runs on north, so it is a real lake, not a pond. On the county's campground map, site 23 sits at the tip of the point south of sites 24-26, with open grass and riprap between it and the water (about 15-20 m on NAIP) and no road between, so it is lakefront. Sites 24-26 sit between the main road and a gravel shore drive, which runs between them and the water: lakeview. Site 27, further north, has the main road between it and the shore: view. Site 22 is on the edge of the boat-ramp lot, which is day use. Site 21 is beside the drainage channel (about 20-25 m wide), not the lake. Sites 1-20, the electric loop south of the channel, are in trees against farm fields with no water view. The map doesn't say which sites are electric, so I can't tell whether 23 is one of the $25 sites. The lakefront value stands on site 23 alone; if AWH wants the value to describe the electric loop, it is not waterfront.

SITE COUNT: the county text says 46 sites (22 electric, 24 primitive), but its campground map numbers only 1-27. I kept 46 from the text, with the gap in sites.note. The other 19 primitive sites may be open tent or overflow areas that aren't numbered.
FIT: no length is posted. NAIP shows trailers and motorhomes parked along the electric loop (sites 1-20), which has gravel spurs on level ground, so a 23-ft motorhome looks fine. No caveat proposed.
SEASON: none posted (park hours 6:00 am - 10:30 pm only). No closure posted.

PIN OK: 41.06357,-90.96824 sits at the north end of the electric loop, within about 50 m of the sites. Phone OK: the stored 319-753-8260 is Des Moines County Conservation's main contact number (https://desmoinescounty.iowa.gov/conservation/). Website: the county page has the rates and the map, so it could be listed first, ahead of mycountyparks.
